facts.text: Major private employers in Guelph include auto-parts maker Linamar, The Co-operators insurance group and RWDI, a wind and environmental engineering firm headquartered in the city.
A federal government investment in Linamar is creating 1,500 new jobs and securing more than 8,000 others in Guelph.
facts.publisher: Government of Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development)

facts.text: Advanced manufacturing counts 360 businesses in Guelph, in an economy anchored on advanced manufacturing, agri-food, life sciences, environmental innovation and technology.

overview: Guelph reached 143,740 residents in the 2021 Census, a 9.1% rise from 131,794 in 2016. The median age is 38.4 and the median household income in 2020 was $93,000, so the city combines a young population with strong spending power.

Those residents live in 56,480 occupied dwellings on a compact 87.43 square kilometres, and the job base leans on advanced manufacturing, with 360 businesses in that sector alone. For a local firm, Guelph offers a dense, growing and relatively affluent customer pool.
